headline: Amazon online store sales up just 2% as Prime Day shifts to Q2; North America margin improves but EPS misses.

metrics.comp_label: Online stores sales growth (ex-FX if available)

guidance_note: Q4 2026: net sales $240-247B (+12-16%), midpoint below ~$244.5B consensus; operating income $28.5-33.5B; ad growth seen back to high teens.
key_messages: Online stores sales ~$68.5B, +2%; Prime Day moved into Q2, which Amazon says cut Q3 growth by ~400bps.
North America sales $112.9B (+6%); segment operating income $8.7B vs $4.8B, margin ~7.7%.
Third-party seller services $46.5B, +9% (+10% ex-FX); advertising ~$19.6B, +11% (12% ex-FX), down from 26% in Q2.
Amazon cites fastest Q3 deliveries ever: 1.5B+ items same-day/overnight; grocery gross sales near $250B over trailing 12 months.
macro_read: After stripping out the Prime Day timing shift, US online goods demand looks steady, not weak; growth leaning on grocery and essentials fits a cautious consumer. The holiday outlook was guided conservatively.
